questions.question: What was the average headline CPI inflation rate for 2023-24 and what factors drove its movement according to the RBI Annual Report?
contexts: Headline CPI inflation moderated to an average of 5.4 per cent in 2023-24 from 6.7 per cent in 2022-23. The easing was primarily driven by a substantial softening in core inflation (CPI excluding food and fuel) to 4.3 per cent, reflecting the impact of monetary policy tightening and easing global supply chain pressures. However, food inflation remained elevated and volatile, registering repeated supply shocks due to erratic weather patterns.
questions.ground_truth: Headline CPI inflation moderated to an average of 5.4 per cent in 2023-24 from 6.7 per cent in 2022-23. The disinflation was driven by core inflation easing to 4.3 per cent due to monetary policy actions, while food inflation remained volatile due to weather shocks.
questions.actual_answer: Headline CPI inflation averaged 5.4 per cent in 2023-24, down from 6.7 per cent in 2022-23. questions.question: What was India's Current Account Deficit (CAD) as a percentage of GDP in 2023-24 compared to 2022-23?
contexts: India's current account deficit (CAD) narrowed sharply to US$ 23.2 billion (0.7 per cent of GDP) in 2023-24 from US$ 67.0 billion (2.0 per cent of GDP) in 2022-23. The compression in CAD was supported by lower merchandise trade deficit and robust growth in services exports and remittances.

questions.topic: Central Bank Digital Currency (CBDC / e-Rupee) Pilot (2023-24)
questions.question: What progress was made in the pilot implementations of the Central Bank Digital Currency (e₹) during 2023-24?
contexts: During 2023-24, the Reserve Bank expanded the Central Bank Digital Currency (CBDC) pilots in both wholesale (e₹-W) and retail (e₹-R) segments. The retail pilot (e₹-R) expanded to include over 4.6 million users and 4 lakh merchants across 16 banks in multiple cities. Interoperability with UPI QR codes was introduced in July 2023, significantly boosting merchant acceptance.
questions.ground_truth: The RBI expanded both wholesale and retail CBDC pilots, with e₹-R reaching over 4.6 million users and 4 lakh merchants across 16 banks. UPI QR code interoperability was launched in July 2023.
questions.actual_answer: During 2023-24, the Reserve Bank expanded its CBDC pilots in both the wholesale (e₹-W) and retail (e₹-R) segments. The retail pilot grew to over 4.6 million users and 4 lakh merchants across 16 banks in multiple cities. Interoperability with UPI QR codes was introduced in July 2023, which significantly boosted merchant acceptance.

questions.question: What was the overall Priority Sector Lending (PSL) target for commercial banks and did they achieve it in 2023-24?
contexts: All Scheduled Commercial Banks are mandated to achieve an overall Priority Sector Lending (PSL) target of 40 per cent of Adjusted Net Bank Credit (ANBC) or Credit Equivalent Amount of Off-Balance Sheet Exposure (CEOBE), whichever is higher. As on March 31, 2024, public and private sector banks collectively achieved an overall PSL achievement ratio of 44.7 per cent.
questions.ground_truth: The mandated PSL target for Scheduled Commercial Banks was 40 per cent of ANBC or CEOBE. As of March 31, 2024, banks achieved an overall PSL ratio of 44.7 per cent.

Yes, they exceeded it: as of March 31, 2024, public and private sector banks collectively achieved an overall PSL ratio of 44.7 per cent.
